newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia port strike blocks private coffee exports.
newsitem.headline: Colombia port strike blocks private coffee exports.

text.p: The seven-day-old strike by dock workers in Colombia's main Pacific coast port has blocked the export of 145,000 60-kg bags of private coffee exports, the head of a private exporters association said Tuesday.

The National Coffee Growers' Federation said last week that 160,000 60-kg bags of its export coffee had been paralyzed by the stoppage, taking the total of private and federation coffee locked in port to more than 300,000 bags.

Gabriel Rosas Vega, head of the private Colombian Coffee Exporters Association, said some of the coffee blocked in Buenaventura, the shipment point for 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports, had been scheduled for December delivery and the remainder for January. He was unable to give percentages.

"Quite simply we have no capacity to respond to this emergency. Some of the coffee was for December delivery and we're worried that we will now face sanctions (from buyers) for defaulting on the contracts," Rosas said.
A private exporter estimated one-quarter of the private exports blocked in port were December shipments.

The strike, which dockers launched to press for higher wages and sickness and injury benefits, has also paralyzed all Colombia's sugar exports. About 27,000 tonnes in bulk containers and sacks is currently blocked in port.
